name: HUD Small Area Fair Market Rents (SAFMR)
gap: Rent benchmarks by bedroom count are currently sourced from Zillow ZORI (ZIP-weighted to NTA, metro-tier blended) and RentCast (capped at 31 requests/month, 24h cooldown — see app/sources/rentcast.py). Neither gives a cheap, generalizable-to-any-US-ZIP, by-bedroom-count rent reference that investment.py's BEDROOM_RENT_FACTOR logic could cross-check against or fall back to when RentCast's tiny budget is exhausted.
coverage: national — HUD designates Fair Market Rents for every US county/metro area; Small Area FMRs (ZIP-level) are 'calculated for ZIP Codes within Metropolitan Areas' per HUD's own ArcGIS dataset description, including the New York, NY HUD Metro FMR Area (covers NYC's 5 boroughs), with standard (metro-wide) FMRs for the rest of the country. Exact count of SAFMR-designated metros not verified first-hand this run.
granularity: ZIP code (SAFMR) within SAFMR-designated metros; county/metro-wide FMR elsewhere
update_frequency: annual, published each federal fiscal year (Oct 1), typically released ~August for the upcoming FY
history_available: NOT VERIFIED — search results didn't give a start year for the SAFMR series specifically (as opposed to standard FMRs, which go back decades). SAFMR is a newer, separate program from standard FMR, so its own history is likely shorter; confirm actual start year on huduser.gov before relying on it for a multi-year backtest.
license: Produced directly by HUD, a US federal agency, for the Section 8 program -> federal government work, no copyright (17 U.S.C. 105) is the expected default, but NOT independently verified first-hand: huduser.gov was unreachable from this session (network policy blocked it, see note below), so this is inferred from the agency/program, not confirmed on HUD's own ToS/disclaimer page. (A third-party site, fairmarketrentmap.com, wraps the same data behind a paid API; that one is NOT the source to use.)
cost: free, no rate limit observed on the bulk files
access_method: bulk XLSX/CSV download from huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html (one file/year, all ZIPs + bedroom sizes + 90%/110% payment standards); also mirrored on HUD's ArcGIS Open Data hub (services.arcgis.com/.../HUD_PDR_Small_Area_Fair_Market_Rents/FeatureServer) and catalog.data.gov as CSV/GeoJSON/Shapefile. HUD does have a separate authenticated API (requires an account + access token) for other HUD datasets, but SAFMR's own bulk files don't require that — use those, not the API.

correlation.notes: app/research/evaluate_series.py does not exist yet (Phase 4 not built). Qualitatively, SAFMR is explicitly calibrated to be a rent-level proxy (40th/50th percentile of actual market rents by ZIP and bedroom count from ACS/AHS microdata), so it should track ZORI closely by construction, but with a ~1-year lag and administrative smoothing rather than real-time market movement.

recommendation: Add as a new `neighborhood`-kind source (e.g. app/sources/hud_safmr.py) that downloads the annual SAFMR file, filters to the metro(s) in scope, and maps ZIP -> NTA using the same ZIP-weighting approach zillow_research.py already uses for ZORI. Its expected federal public-domain licensing (not yet confirmed first-hand — huduser.gov was unreachable this run), true national coverage (fits the project's US-generalization goal far better than RentCast's 5-area budget), and native by-bedroom-count breakdown make it a strong complement to ZORI/RentCast: a free, unlimited, no-login rent reference to fall back on or sanity-check against, especially outside NYC where RentCast's area list doesn't reach at all. Before implementing: confirm on huduser.gov that there's no ToS/login wall on the bulk files and check the actual SAFMR start year, since both were unverified this run. Annual cadence means it won't capture short-term rent swings, so it should supplement rather than replace RentCast listings-derived estimates where those exist.
